title: Derived subgroup and dominant finite commutator word over any field
statement:
Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be a smooth geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Closed subgroups are [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. The smallest closed subgroup $D(G)\subseteq G$ through which the commutator morphism $(x,y)\mapsto xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ factors exists. It is normal, smooth and geometrically connected. For some integer $r\geq1$, the morphism
$$w_r:G^{2r}\longrightarrow D(G),\qquad (x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_r,y_r)\longmapsto\prod_{j=1}^r x_jy_jx_j^{-1}y_j^{-1}$$
has dense image in the underlying topological space. Here the powers and products are over $k$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every extension field $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], the inclusion identifies $D(G)_K$ with $D(G_K)$. Every homomorphism from $G$ to a commutative affine $k$-group scheme of finite type is trivial on $D(G)$, and the represented fppf quotient $G/D(G)$ of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] is commutative. These assertions include the commutative and trivial groups, for which $D(G)=1=\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Corollary 6.19(b),(d),(e), Propositions 6.20(a) and 6.21, printed pp.129-130; Theorem 16.58, general-case derived-group reduction, p.345.

proof.text: Put $X=G\times_kG$, $o=(e,e)$ and $c(x,y)=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$. These are a pointed affine finite-type scheme and a morphism with $c(o)=e$, by the group operations. For every $k$-algebra $R$, $c(x,y)^{-1}=c(y,x)$, so its image is inversion stable. The projections $X\to G$ are smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Thus $X$ is geometrically reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. It is geometrically connected: after any field extension both factors are connected, and [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components] says their product has one connected component. The identity tuple ensures nonemptiness.

source.place: Section 2h, Propositions 2.46 and 2.48, pp.54–55; Corollary 6.19(b), p.129: hypotheses for the commutator-generated subgroup

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ let $w_n:G^{2n}\to G$ be the product of $n$ commutators and put $A=k[G]$, $B_n=k[G^{2n}]$, $I_n=\ker(w_n^*:A\to B_n)$ and $I=\bigcap_{n\geq1}I_n$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup] to $(X,o,c)$. It gives $D=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, the smallest closed subgroup through which $c$ factors, affine of finite type, geometrically reduced and geometrically connected. Since $D$ is a finite-type group scheme and geometrically reduced, [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] makes it smooth. This establishes existence and the geometric assertions without assuming $k$ perfect.

source.place: Propositions 2.46, 2.48, pp.54–55; Proposition 6.18 and Corollary 6.19(b), p.129

proof.text: Here is the scalar-extension calculation used below. For a field extension $K/k$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies the pullback of $w_n$ with the coordinate map $w_n^*\otimes_kK:A\otimes_kK\to B_n\otimes_kK$. Choose a $k$-basis $(b_j)$ of $K$. Each tensor is a unique finite sum $\sum_j a_j\otimes b_j$, and its image is zero exactly when every $w_n^*(a_j)$ is zero. Therefore $\ker(w_{n,K}^*)=I_n\otimes_kK$, viewed as an ideal in $A\otimes_kK$. The same coefficient calculation identifies $(A/I_n)\otimes_kK$ with $(A\otimes_kK)/(I_n\otimes_kK)$ and reflects equality of extended subspaces of $A$ (compare coefficients of $a\otimes1$). No exchange of an infinite intersection with tensor product is used.

source.place: Proposition 2.47, p.55, scalar-extension calculation made explicit for individual kernels

proof.text: By [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique], choose an algebraic closure $\bar k/k$. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), $G_{\bar k}$ is smooth; it is connected by the given geometric connectedness. Apply [lem-sfb-pointed-word-kernel-stabilization] over $\bar k$, with source group and target group both $G_{\bar k}$, the exponent $2$, and pointed map $c_{\bar k}$. It gives $N\geq1$ such that the kernels of the $w_{n,\bar k}$ are equal for all $n\geq N$. By step 3 and reflection of equality there, $I_n=I_N$ for all $n\geq N$. Inserting identity pairs gives $I_{n+1}\subseteq I_n$, so $I=I_N$. In particular $w_N$ factors through $v_N:G^{2N}\to D$ and $v_N^*:A/I_N\to B_N$ is injective.

source.place: Proposition 6.20(a), p.130; Section 2h scalar extension, p.55

proof.text: For any field extension $K/k$, construct the minimal commutator subgroup of $G_K$ by the same generated-map lemma: the pointed map is still inversion stable. Step 3 gives its defining ideal $\bigcap_n(I_n\otimes_kK)=I_N\otimes_kK$, since the descending chain is constant from $N$ onward. The quotient identification in step 3 therefore identifies this subgroup with $D_K$ as a closed subgroup of $G_K$. In particular for $K=\bar k$, [lem-sfb-pointed-word-kernel-stabilization] says that $v_{N,\bar k}$ has dense image. The projection $D_{\bar k}\to D$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum]. Every nonempty open of $D$ has a nonempty inverse image, which meets $\operatorname{im}(v_{N,\bar k})$; its image in $D$ is in $\operatorname{im}(v_N)$. Thus $v_N$ has dense image. Take $r=N$.

source.place: Proposition 2.47, p.55; Corollary 6.19(a), p.129, and Proposition 6.20(a), p.130

proof.text: For each $k$-algebra $R$, each $g\in G(R)$ and $d\in D(R)$, the commutator $[g,d]$ belongs to $D(R)$ because the commutator morphism factors through $D$. Since $D(R)$ is a subgroup, $gdg^{-1}=[g,d]d$ belongs to $D(R)$. Replacing $g$ by $g^{-1}$ gives the inverse inclusion. Hence $D$ is normal in the functor-of-points sense of [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. This proves scheme-theoretic normality over arbitrary algebras, including nonreduced ones.

source.place: Proposition 6.18, p.129, normality of the commutator-generated subgroup

proof.text: Let $f:G\to C$ be a homomorphism to a commutative affine finite-type $k$-group scheme. It kills every commutator by the group identity, so $f\circ w_N$ is identity valued. For $j:D\hookrightarrow G$ and $a\in k[C]$, the difference between $(f\circ j)^*(a)$ and the pullback by the identity-valued map $D\to C$ becomes zero under the injective map $v_N^*$ from step 4. The difference is therefore zero. By the coordinate description of affine morphisms [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $f|_D$ is the identity-valued homomorphism.

source.place: Corollary 6.19(d), p.129, with the finite-word coordinate verification

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] to the closed normal finite-type affine subgroup $D\subseteq G$. It gives the represented fppf quotient $q:G\to Q=G/D$ with kernel $D$ and local surjectivity. Given two sections of $Q$ over a $k$-algebra $R$, lift each to a section of $G$ after fppf covers and refine the two covers to lift both. Their commutator is the image of a commutator in $G$, hence is the identity since that commutator lies in $D=\ker q$. Since $Q$ is a sheaf, the two original sections commute. This holds for every $R$ and proves commutativity of the quotient group scheme. If $G$ is commutative, $c=e$ factors through the identity subgroup; minimality gives $D=1$. This includes $G=1$, and $w_1$ is then the identity-valued map onto $\operatorname{Spec}k$, with dense image.

source.place: Proposition 6.18 and Corollary 6.19(d), p.129; quotient sheaf of Section 5j, pp.116–118

proof_origin.place: Section 2h, Propositions 2.46–2.48, pp.54–55; Proposition 6.18, Corollary 6.19(a),(b),(d), and Proposition 6.20(a), pp.129–130; field-extension kernel argument expanded explicitly.
